items.stem: What is the main job of an engineering drawing?

options.text: To be framed and admired as a work of art
To use up extra paper in the design room
To communicate a design so someone else can build it
To keep the design a secret from other people

items.explanation: A drawing exists to move an idea from your head into someone else's hands. Its job is communication, not decoration.

items.stem: A drawing is made to scale so a big object fits on paper. What stays true when it is drawn to scale?

options.text: Every part shrinks by the same amount, so the proportions stay correct
Only the tallest part is drawn and the rest are left off
The exact colors of the real object are copied
The drawing ends up larger than the real object

items.explanation: Scaling shrinks every part by the same amount, so a part twice as long in real life is still twice as long on paper. That is what keeps the drawing honest.

items.stem: You need to draw a full-size house so it fits on one sheet of paper. Which scale makes the most sense?

options.text: Full size, one to one, so nothing is shrunk
One unit on paper stands for 100 units in real life
Scaled up, five to one, so the drawing is bigger than the house
No scale at all, just a quick sketch

items.explanation: A house is far too big for full size, so you shrink it. A scale like 1 unit for 100 fits the whole house on the page while keeping it readable.

items.stem: What does a scale bar on a drawing tell a builder?

options.text: The name of the person who made the drawing
Which colors to paint the finished object
How heavy the finished object will be
What one unit on the drawing stands for in real life

items.explanation: A scale bar is the key that lets any builder turn the drawing back into real sizes, without ever meeting the designer.

items.stem: Two builders get the same drawing with a scale and measurements, but nothing on it is labeled. What is the most likely problem?

options.text: The drawing is far too colorful to follow
They cannot begin, because a drawing with no labels also has no scale
They may put parts in the wrong place, since nothing names what each part is
The finished object will come out the wrong color

items.explanation: Labels name each part and show how it fits. Without them, the sizes may be right but the parts can still end up in the wrong places.

items.stem: One drawing of a chair is a beautiful, shaded painting with no measurements. Another is plain but has a scale, dimensions, and labels. Which is the better engineering drawing?

options.text: The plain one, because a builder could make it exactly
The painting, because it looks more realistic and finished
The painting, because it clearly took much more effort
Neither, because a chair is too simple to need a drawing

items.explanation: An engineering drawing is judged by whether someone can build from it. The plain drawing communicates the real sizes; the painting only looks good.

items.stem: You are drawing a tiny watch gear so small it is hard to see. Which choice would help you show it clearly?

options.text: Shrink it further with a 1 unit for 100 scale
Scale it up so the drawing is larger than the real gear
Leave the scale off so no one gets confused
Draw it in several bright colors

items.explanation: Scale works both ways. For something tiny, you scale up and draw it bigger than real life so every tooth is clear, then note the scale.

items.stem: Which of these is a model an engineer might use to communicate a design?

options.text: A song written about the design
An idea kept only inside your head
A scaled drawing or a small build of the design
A completely blank sheet of paper

items.explanation: A model is any representation that helps others understand an idea. A scaled drawing or a small build both let other people see and build the design.

items.stem: A drawing shows a doghouse where the door is almost as big as the whole wall, even though the real door is small. What is wrong?

options.text: The drawing simply needs more color and shading to look finished
The scale bar has been drawn in a font that is too fancy
Nothing is wrong, because the size of the door on paper does not matter
The proportions are wrong, so the build will not match the real doghouse

items.explanation: In a scaled drawing every part must keep its true proportion. A door drawn too big means the builder makes it wrong, even if the scale is correct.

items.stem: A classmate says, "My design is amazing, so it does not matter if anyone else understands my drawing." What is the best engineering response?

options.text: A great idea is only useful if others can understand and build it, so the drawing has to communicate
You are right; if the idea is good enough, the drawing can be skipped
Only the person who dreamed up the design should ever be allowed to build it
Drawings are only there for decoration, so it truly does not matter

items.explanation: Good engineers do not just build great ideas; they communicate them so others can build them too. A drawing no one else understands cannot do that.
